description: Sabotages for how a file is opened and held. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format.

sabotages.name: the file is opened with write access
sabotages.why: TW-D-3 says read-only. A hold with write access still opens, still shares, and still answers the observer's queries, so only a new open that denies write sharing -- which collides with a writer -- can tell.

sabotages.name: the path is converted lossily
sabotages.why: A name with an unpaired surrogate is a real NTFS name and not valid Unicode. Replacing the surrogate with U+FFFD names a different file, which does not exist.

sabotages.name: an open failure loses its Win32 code
sabotages.why: The caller tells a missing file from a sharing violation by the code. Wrapping the error in a new one keeps the kind and drops the number.
replace:
let endpoint = UnassociatedEndpoint::open(path.to_os_string(), true, false, 0)
            .map_err(|error| io::Error::new(error.kind(), "open failed"))?;

sabotages.name: the length is the bytes allocated rather than the end of file
sabotages.why: Allocation is rounded up to the allocation unit, and a small file reports its whole cluster. Only a length that is not a multiple of it can tell the two apart.

sabotages.name: the length is cut to 32 bits
sabotages.why: Every file under 4 GiB reads the same either way, so only a file past that can show it.

sabotages.name: the length is read once and remembered
sabotages.why: A cache returns the right answer until the file changes, so only a read after a write or a shrink can tell.

sabotages.name: an offset equal to the length is refused
sabotages.why: TW-D-3 says beyond the length. A parent that stopped at the end of the file must be able to restart there, so the boundary is where the comparison goes wrong.

sabotages.name: an offset past the length is accepted
sabotages.why: The check is the item. Without it every other test of an accepted offset still passes.

sabotages.name: the offset is not kept
sabotages.why: A validated offset that is then forgotten leaves the restart with nowhere to resume.

sabotages.name: the offset is compared as 32 bits
sabotages.why: Every file under 4 GiB compares the same either way.
replace: if offset as u32 > len as u32 {

sabotages.name: control: the comparison is written the other way round
sabotages.why: len < offset is offset > len, so the two are one check.

sabotages.name: control: the length is read through standard_info
sabotages.why: file_len is defined as standard_info's len, so the two are one read spelled twice.

sabotages.name: control: the path is converted through OsString::from
sabotages.why: The same lossless conversion spelled another way. A test that catches it is asserting how the conversion is written, not what it does.
